slides.texte_overlay:
Lessons from good fathers
every man should learn
Show up, again and again. Good fathers are remembered less for big moments than for being there every single day. Presence is the real gift.
Stay calm when things go wrong. A broken glass, a bad grade, a dented car. How you react teaches people around you how to handle problems.
Teach by doing. Fix things together, cook together, work together. People learn far more from watching you than from listening to you.
Say "I'm proud of you" out loud. Many men never heard it from their dads. Saying it to your friends, brothers and future kids changes lives.
Keep learning to have more to share. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and I love passing stories on to younger people.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. I love passing stories on to younger people.

slides.texte_overlay: Admit when you're wrong. A man who says sorry to his family teaches them that strength and humility go together. Humility is strength.
Make time for fun. Games, trips, jokes, silly traditions. The happiest memories are often the simplest ones you created together.
